title: Aloo Gobi
subtitle: Dry spiced potato and cauliflower curry
excerpt: Potato and cauliflower cooked together with onion, garlic, ginger, and a blend of warm spices until tender and fragrant. A dry Punjabi curry that is as good at room temperature as it is fresh from the pan.

recipe.sourceNotes: Aloo gobi is a Punjabi dish that became one of the most recognisable vegetarian curries in British Indian restaurants. It was popularised in Britain through films (it features prominently in Bend It Like Beckham) and cookbooks from the 1990s onwards. The key characteristic is that it is a dry sabzi (vegetable dish), not a curry with a sauce. The potato and cauliflower should be tender and spice-coated, with no excess liquid. Add only a little water if the pan gets dry, not enough to make a gravy.

recipeTools.notes: Or a wide, heavy-based frying pan with a lid.

content.text: Cut everything to the same size for even cooking: potato pieces and cauliflower florets both around 3 cm. The cumin seeds in the hot oil release their flavour quickly: add the onion before they burn. Cover the pan while the vegetables cook so they steam from the inside while browning on the outside.

items.preparation: peeled and cut into 3 cm pieces

content.text: Heat the oil in a wide, heavy-based pan over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and fry for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 minute. Add the turmeric, ground cumin, ground coriander, and chilli powder. Cook for 1 minute.

Add the potato and cauliflower. Stir to coat in the spices. Add 3 tablespoons of water. Cover and cook over medium heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are completely tender. Add a splash more water if the pan dries out.
Stir in the garam masala and salt. Scatter with fresh coriander. Serve with rice, naan, or flatbread.
